faq_heading: Questions people ask when choosing an SEO option

faqs.q: What is the main difference between an AI SEO agent, an SEO agency and an SEO tool?
faqs.a: A tool gives you data and drafts, but your team still does the work. An agency does the work with people on their schedule. An AI SEO agent does the daily work itself, from research to publishing, indexing and tracking, and reports to you.

faqs.q: Is an AI SEO agent better than an SEO agency?
faqs.a: Not always. An agency is better for complex technical fixes, large site migrations or digital PR. An AI SEO agent is better when the gap is steady, daily publishing on buyer topics that nobody on your team has time to own.

faqs.q: Can I just buy an SEO tool and do it myself?
faqs.a: Yes, if someone on your team has a few hours every week to research, write, publish and check results. Most B2B founders and sales heads don't, which is why the tool ends up unused.

faqs.q: Will content from an AI SEO agent rank on Google?
faqs.a: Google says it rewards helpful, reliable content however it is made. The agent writes from your approved facts and real examples, answers the buyer's question first and links pages into a topic cluster, which is what helps pages rank.

faqs.q: Can I use an AI SEO agent together with an agency or a tool?
faqs.a: Yes. Many teams keep an agency for technical audits or link building and let the agent handle daily content, indexing and weekly reporting. The agent can also use the tool data you already pay for.
